newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine could extend '96 budget to July - Kuchma.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine could extend '96 budget to July - Kuchma.

text.p: President Leonid Kuchma, struggling to get this year's budget passed to pave the way for a multi-billion-dollar International Monetary Fund loan, has said Ukraine may have to manage without a budget until July.

Speaking to reporters in a television interview broadcast late on Tuesday, he said: "Clearly we can live with the proposal that for the first half of the year we live with the old budget...and the second half will be based on the new budget".

The budget and a package of nine tax reform laws to underpin it are stuck between government -- still working on a revised version -- and a largely conservative parliament, which is reluctant to approve tough economic reforms.
"Considering the budget situation, and discussions over the budget in parliament, we see that we have painted ourselves into a corner and can go neither here nor there," Kuchma said.
"We have to reach a mutual understanding at meetings between government and parliament, because living without the basic economic law of the nation is impossible," Kuchma said.

Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko urged parliament on Tuesday to pass the budget and tax laws by the end of April, but Kuchma said realistically it would take two to three months to make the tax laws effective.

Kuchma on Tuesday appointed banker Serhiy Tyhypko as deputy prime minister in charge of the economy to replace Viktor Pynzenyk, a leading reformer who quit this week in anger over budget and tax reform delays.
Acceptance of the budget, agreed with the International Monetary Fund, would pave the way for a multi-billion dollar, long-term credit from the IMF.
